14cd7fc0884e5b1043a7ceff2dfca147ba8a0550.summary: Europol reports an international operation led by the FBI, with Europol and J-CAT support, that seized internet domains used to sell the Warzone RAT, a remote access trojan that let buyers secretly watch and control victims' computers. Two suspects were arrested on 7 February in Malta and Nigeria and are accused of selling the malware and supporting its users. Countries listed as involved include Australia, Canada, Croatia, Finland, Germany, Malta, the Netherlands, Nigeria, Romania and the United States.

144ff3f73f70ab2e208db4560e9e6562a6ca1ada.summary: Analysis of the DDG.Mining.Botnet Monero-mining botnet, which targets Redis and SSH services. It covers version 3011 (new wallet, cloud config, scan-traffic surge on Redis and SSH ports, Crontab persistence) and later updates: 3011 x86_64 sample, new miner builds, and version 3012 released 12 June 2018 with a new main C2. Wallet payouts on two mining pools are reported.

14ed9f4cb898b47864e36e066426fc1ec5b58e46.summary: SANS blog post (2022-10-05) on the leaked and cracked Brute Ratel C4 post-exploitation toolkit (v1.2.2), which spread across English- and Russian-speaking cybercrime forums. It says the tool can generate shellcode that many EDR and AV products miss, and that ransomware affiliates will likely use it. Sophos saw it alongside Cobalt Strike at an ALPHV ransomware engagement in July 2022. A Russian-speaking group called Molecules cracked the licence check.
